0.long_answer: Botulinum toxin type A is the specific neurotoxic protein produced by Clostridium botulinum that is commonly used as the first-line treatment for blepharospasm. This treatment works by selectively inhibiting the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, thereby reducing the involuntary contractions or spasms of the eyelid muscles. Its targeted effect makes it highly effective in managing the symptoms associated with blepharospasm, and it remains the most preferred option given its established safety and efficacy profile.
